name: Protectorate of the Western Regions
alt: Protectorate General of the Western Regions
Chief Official of the Western Regions

predecessors.name: Xiongnu
predecessors.text: the Northern and Southern routes of the Western Regions, until the Rizhu King of the Right submitted to the Han

ledger.x: 60 BCE: Zheng Ji becomes the first protector-general of the Western Regions, with headquarters at Wulei.
51 BCE: the Wusun submit to the Han.
23 CE: the Wusun tie lapses with the protectorate.
23 CE: the protectorate is abandoned in the Wang Mang years.
73: Han and Xiongnu fight for the Western Regions again.
74: Kashgar comes under Chinese rule ('by 74 CE', same sentence as Khotan).
89: the Han-Xiongnu contest for the Western Regions ends.
91: Ban Chao takes Kucha and the Protector General's seat.
91: the rest of the Tarim Basin, apart from Yanqi, is drawn as Han.
91: the Protector General sits at Qiuci (Kucha).
94: Ban Chao defeats Yanqi and the whole basin submits.
107: the Qiang rising ends the protectorate.
176: the Han presence in the Tarim ends.
335: Zhang Jun's Former Liang marches across the sands and the oasis states submit.
335: the revived protectorate is headquartered at Gaochang (Turfan).
439: the protectorate ends with the Sixteen Kingdoms.

wars.name: Han–Xiongnu War
wars.outcome: The Han under Dou Gu and Ban Chao take Shanshan, Khotan and Kashgar (73-74); the Western Regions are 'a heavily contested region during the Han-Xiongnu War until 89 AD'.

wars.name: Ban Chao's conquest of the Tarim Basin
wars.outcome: Khotan and Kashgar by 74; rebellions in Kashgar (80, 87) and Yarkand (88) crushed; Ban Chao Protector General at Qiuci in 91; Yanqi defeated in 94 and over fifty kingdoms give hostages.

wars.name: Kushan–Han clash of 90
wars.outcome: The Kushans, refused a Han princess, 'marched on Ban Chao in 90 CE with a force of 70,000 but were defeated by the smaller Chinese force'; no border moved.

wars.name: Qiang uprisings of 107
wars.outcome: Qiang risings in the Hexi Corridor and Guanzhong on 29 July 107: Duan Xi was killed and the protectorate abandoned.

wars.name: Former Liang's expedition into the Tarim
wars.outcome: Zhang Jun's forces 'marched across the sands and expanded his territory' in 335; the oasis states such as Kucha submitted and the protectorate was revived at Gaochang.

certainty.note: Every frontier is a desert-oasis reach: the Tarim rim, Turfan-Hami and the Pamir foot are approximate, defined by which city-states submitted.
